harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Established an AIDE-based file integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 10). Installed aide, added an explicit /etc FIPSR rule to aide.conf, initialized the database (36,014 entries), activated it as /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, and recorded a sha256 checksum plus creation timestamp for the baseline artifact. Verified detection works end-to-end: aide --check reports clean against the untouched baseline, flags an injected content change to /etc/hosts (exit code 4, size/hash diff shown) and returns clean again after the file was restored. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and a clean aide --check, rebooted node1 natively, confirmed the boot_id changed, and reconfirmed the AIDE database checksum and a clean aide --check post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (RHEL 10.0) and sudo availability
Diagnosed and fixed a dnf GPG-key import failure by manually running rpm --import on /etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-redhat-release
Appended an explicit '/etc FIPSR' rule to /etc/aide.conf for full content/permission/hash coverage of /etc
Ran aide --init to build the baseline database and copied aide.db.new.gz to the active aide.db.gz
Recorded aide.db.gz.sha256 checksum and a baseline-established-at.txt UTC timestamp
Ran aide --check to confirm the fresh baseline reports no differences
Injected a benign content change into /etc/hosts, ran aide --check to confirm detection (exit code 4, hash/size diff reported), restored the file, and reconfirmed a clean check

Captured pre-restart boot_id and AIDE health, issued a native reboot on node1 with the ack returned before disconnection, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified the AIDE database checksum and a clean aide --check post-restart

evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and configured to cover /etc
evidence.summary: dnf install of aide succeeded after fixing GPG key import; aide.conf shows an explicit '/etc FIPSR' rule added alongside existing granular /etc rules

evidence.requirement: Integrity baseline database initialized and activated
evidence.summary: aide --init created a database with 36,014 entries; it was copied to /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz as the active baseline, with a sha256 checksum and timestamp recorded alongside it

evidence.requirement: Baseline correctly reports clean state with no prior changes
evidence.summary: aide --check --config=/etc/aide.conf exited 0 with 'AIDE found NO differences between database and filesystem. Looks okay!!' immediately after baseline creation

evidence.requirement: Baseline can identify later changes to /etc files (core task purpose)
evidence.summary: Appending a line to /etc/hosts caused aide --check to exit 4 and report 'Changed entries: 1' with a full before/after size and SHA512/SHA3-256 diff for /etc/hosts; restoring the file returned aide --check to exit 0 with no differences
Captured boot_id 368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a, verified aide.db.gz.sha256 checksum matched (OK), and ran a clean aide --check before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded a delayed reboot via nohup/disown so the exec call returned 'reboot scheduled, ack returned' prior to the node going down

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Connection timed out twice while node1 was down, then a subsequent poll succeeded and returned boot_id 7007c7f6-b267-4355-9b70-10c0e26035bb, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of the integrity baseline artifact and its function
evidence.summary: After the restart, /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz still matched its recorded sha256 checksum (OK) and aide --check again reported zero differences against the current /etc filesystem state
